   101	/-- **The rank anchor at a witness of the pinned degree.** -/
   102	theorem h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg
   103	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   104	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
   105	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   106	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   107	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
   108	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
   109	    (n : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   110	    (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
   111	    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ))
   112	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
   113	    Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) = 1 := by
   114	  have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := L) W h1
   115	  rw [hW, hχ] at hanchor
   116	  omega
   117	
   118	/-- **THE CONVERSE OF `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1`, WITH THE `h⁰` VALUE READ OFF.** -/
   119	theorem exists_splitting_h0_eq_one_of_mem_chartLocus
   120	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
   121	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)
   122	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   123	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   124	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   125	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0)
   126	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
   127	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
   128	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
   129	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
   130	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
   131	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
   132	        (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
   133	      -- `M` presents the TWISTED fibre class at `t`: this is what ties the conclusion to
   134	      -- `lam`, `m`, `Z` and `t`, and without it the statement is satisfied by `W = 0`.
   135	      PicEtAff.map C L
   136	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
   137	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
   138	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
   139	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M ∧
   140	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) ∧
   141	      Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) = 1 := by
   142	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hWcl, hWh1⟩ := ht
   143	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   144	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   145	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   146	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   147	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   148	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   149	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   150	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   151	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   152	  -- the witness has degree exactly `n`: its class is the presenting class of the twisted
   153	  -- fibre class, whose `classDeg` the ledger computes as `m·d₁ − deg Z = n`.
   154	  have hWdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) := by
   155	    rw [← classDeg_picClass (K := L) W, hWcl,
   156	      classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff C L _ M hM]
   157	    change degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) (Over.testPoint t) = (n : ℤ)
   158	    rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
   159	      degAt_sigmaFamily, hlam, hdeg]
   160	    ring
   161	  -- `χ(𝒪)` transports to the base-changed curve
   162	  have hχL : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ) :=
   163	    chi_relCurve_baseField C L n hχ
   164	  exact ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, W, hM, hWcl, hWdeg,
   165	    h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg n hχL W hWdeg hWh1⟩
   166	
   167	/-- **GAP-2 UNIQUENESS AT A WITNESS OF THE PINNED DEGREE** — the keystone with its `h⁰`
   168	binder discharged rather than assumed. -/
   169	theorem eq_of_picClass_eq_of_deg_of_subsingleton
   170	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   171	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
   172	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   173	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   174	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
   175	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
   176	    (n : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   177	    (W W' : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
   178	    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ))
   179	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1))
   180	    (hWe : 0 ≤ W) (hW'e : 0 ≤ W')
   181	    (hcl : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W') :
   182	    W' = W :=
   183	  Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one (K := L) hWe hW'e hcl
   184	    (h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg n hχ W hW h1)
   185	
   186	/-- **EFFECTIVITY IS FREE ONCE `h⁰ = 1`** — so the locus supplies GAP-2's `hD` too, and not
   187	only its `hone`. -/
   188	theorem exists_effective_picClass_eq_of_h0_eq_one
   189	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   190	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
   191	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   192	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   193	    (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
   194	    (h : Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) = 1) :
   195	    ∃ E : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧
   196	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L E = Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W :=
   197	  exists_effective_of_h0_pos (K := L) W (by omega)
   198	
   199	/-- **THE UNIQUE EFFECTIVE REPRESENTATIVE AT A LOCUS POINT** — the whole of GAP-2's
   200	field-level content, with every one of the keystone's three binders supplied by the locus. -/
   201	theorem existsUnique_effective_of_mem_chartLocus
   202	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
   203	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)
   204	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   205	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   206	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   207	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0)
   208	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
   209	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
   210	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
   211	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
   212	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
   213	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
   214	        (E : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
   215	      -- `M` presents the TWISTED fibre class at `t`, and `E` represents `M` itself.  Without
   216	      -- these two clauses the statement is satisfied by `L = κ(t)`, `E = 0` on any curve.
   217	      PicEtAff.map C L
   218	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
   219	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
   220	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
   221	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L E = M ∧
   222	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L E = (n : ℤ) ∧
   223	      0 ≤ E ∧
   224	        ∀ E' : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E' →
   225	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L E' = M → E' = E := by
   226	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hWcl, hWh1⟩ := ht
   227	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   228	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   229	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   230	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   231	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   232	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   233	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   234	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   235	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   236	  have hWdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) := by
   237	    rw [← classDeg_picClass (K := L) W, hWcl,
   238	      classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff C L _ M hM]
   239	    change degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) (Over.testPoint t) = (n : ℤ)
   240	    rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
   241	      degAt_sigmaFamily, hlam, hdeg]
   242	    ring
   243	  have hχL : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ) :=
   244	    chi_relCurve_baseField C L n hχ
   245	  have hone : Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) = 1 :=
   246	    h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg n hχL W hWdeg hWh1
   247	  -- the effective representative of the SAME class, and its own `h⁰`/vanishing data
   248	  obtain ⟨E, hEe, hEcl⟩ := exists_effective_picClass_eq_of_h0_eq_one W hone
   249	  -- `E` represents `M` too, has the same degree, and inherits `h⁰ = 1`
   250	  have hEM : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L E = M := hEcl.trans hWcl
   251	  have hEone : Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L E) = 1 := by
   252	    rw [h0_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq (K := L) hEcl]; exact hone
   253	  have hEdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L E = (n : ℤ) :=

   260	/-! ## The non-vacuity check: the strengthened conclusion gives membership back

120	witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.

   123	because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
   124	the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
   125	
   126	## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread
   127	
   128	The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
   129	and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
   130	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
   131	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
   132	on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
   133	class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
   134	against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
   135	condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
   136	with it the openness route.
   137	
   138	Two consequences, both load-bearing:
   139	
   140	* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
   141	  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree
   142	  `m·d₁ − deg Z`, which the constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `+g`.  It is *not* a
   143	  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the
   144	  locus empty for every `g ≥ 1` — see `degAt_chartTwist` and issue I-0514;
   145	  `chartTwist_chartValue` now pins the direction by the kernel);
   146	* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is
   147	  actually needed — the canonical-section normalization `h⁰ = 1`, and GAP-2 uniqueness
   148	  (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`, which does take `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`) — the

   150	  already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one. -/
   151	def IsSplitWitness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

   153	  ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
   154	      (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)

   156	    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)

   158	      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
   159	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
   160	            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   161	                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)

   163	/-! ## The twisted fibre family -/
   164	
   165	variable (C) in
   166	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
   167	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.
   168	
   169	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
   170	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
   171	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
   172	`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
   173	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
   174	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   175	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
   176	  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹
   177	
   178	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
   179	degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
   180	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
   181	`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.
   182	
   183	**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
   184	must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
   185	`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart

   187	`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
   188	`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was

   190	`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
   191	`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.

   193	**An independent confirmation that `+g` is the right target**, worth recording because the
   194	wrong sign survived two sessions: at `deg W = g` the rank anchor
   195	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives, for a
   196	witness with `h¹ = 0`,
   197	`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and

   200	injective.  At `−g` the same anchor gives `h⁰ = 1 − 2g`, negative for `g ≥ 1` — the contradiction

   202	theorem degAt_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   203	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T)
   204	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
   205	    degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
   206	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
   207	  rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
   208	    degAt_sigmaFamily, (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam) K t]
   209	  ring
   210	
   211	/-- **`chartTwist` inverts `chartValue`'s twist** — the sign check, as a theorem rather than a
   212	docstring claim.
   213	
   214	Applying `chartTwist` to a chart value returns the Abel class it came from.  This is the
   215	statement that was FALSE of the earlier definition (which returned
   216	`abelDiv · Σ² · (θᵐ)⁻²`), and it is why the direction is now pinned by the kernel: any future
   217	edit to `chartTwist` that breaks the inversion breaks this lemma.
   218	
   219	Recorded per issue I-0514.  A degree ledger alone does not catch a sign error — the wrong-signed
   220	ledger was internally consistent — but an inversion law does. -/
   221	theorem chartTwist_chartValue {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ)
   222	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   223	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
   224	    chartTwist C m Z T (chartValue C π n m Z T s) = abelDiv C π n T s := by
   225	  rw [chartTwist, chartValue]
   226	  group

   255	/-! ## The datum-layer reading
   256	
   257	The witness clause of `IsSplitWitness` is stated on a presenting Čech class over `C_L`.
   258	The tree's *engine-facing* predicate is stated on a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum`

   265	/-- **The witness clause at a splitting field, in datum form**: for a Čech class `M` over
   266	`C_L`, admitting an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹` is exactly
   267	`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` of any datum presenting `M` — as a class over the base `L` itself,

   270	Note the datum lives over the *field* `L` as base ring, which is the affine base the
   271	engine's `PrimeSpectrum L` has a unique point of; that is why the fibre reading and the
   272	base reading coincide here. -/
   273	theorem exists_witness_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_datum
   274	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   275	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C L π) {M : (relCurve C L).CechPic}
   276	    (hD : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass
   277	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M) :
   278	    (∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
   279	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M
   280	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   281	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1))
   282	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
   283	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hD]
   284	
   285	/-- **Upward closure of the witness clause along a separable extension of the splitting
   286	field** — the substantive half of the (a-amendment)'s "some (equivalently every)".
   287	
   288	If a Čech class `M` over `C_L` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`, then
   289	so does its base change to any finite separable `L'/L`.  This is what makes two splittings
   290	of the same plus class comparable: pass to a common separable extension and compare there,
   291	rather than comparing the two splittings directly.
   292	
   293	Proof: present `M` by a datum `D` over `L` (`exists_cechPicClass_eq`); the witness clause at
   294	`L` is `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L`, which transfers to `L'` by the co-owned separable

   296	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:157` — itself resting only on faithful flatness of a field

   298	theorem exists_witness_of_separable_extension (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
   299	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   300	    {L' : Type u} [Field L'] [Algebra k L'] [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower k L L']
   301	    [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
   302	    (h : ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
   303	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
   304	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   305	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
   306	    ∃ W' : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left).CurveDivisor,
   307	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L' W' = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L') M
   308	        ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   309	            ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left.divisorSheaf L' W') 1) := by
   310	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (B := L) (π := π) M
   311	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
   312	  -- the witness clause at `L` is the datum predicate at `L`: `relCurveMap C L L` acts as
   313	  -- the identity comparison on classes, since it is `Spec` of the identity algebra map.
   314	  have hid : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass := by
   315	    have : relCurveMap C L L = 𝟙 (relCurve C L) := by
   316	      rw [relCurveMap]
   317	      have hom : overSpecMap (k := k) L L = 𝟙 (overSpec k L) :=
   318	        Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simp)
   319	      rw [hom, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id]
   320	      rfl
   321	    rw [this, Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
   322	    rfl
   323	  have hL : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := ⟨W, by rw [hid, hD, hW], hW1⟩
   324	  -- transfer along the separable extension, then read it back as a witness clause
   325	  obtain ⟨W', hW', hW1'⟩ :=
   326	    (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable L L').mp hL
   327	  exact ⟨W', by rw [hW', hD], hW1'⟩

   330	
   331	/-- **`chartLocus` is compatible with restriction of the class**: the twist commutes with
   332	`picEtMap`, so restricting `λ` along a morphism of tests restricts the twisted family too.

   334	This is `sigmaFamily_natural` + `thetaFamily_natural` and nothing else; it is stated

   337	theorem picEtMap_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   338	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) :
   339	    picEtMap C f (chartTwist C m Z T lam)
   340	      = chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam) := by
   341	  rw [chartTwist, chartTwist, map_mul, map_inv, map_mul, map_pow,
   342	    sigmaFamily_natural, thetaFamily_natural]
   343	
   344	/-- **`chartLocus` pulls back into `chartLocus`** — transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6, in the
   345	form the assembly consumes.
   346	
   347	For `f : T' ⟶ T` and `t : T'.left`, membership of `t` in the pulled-back locus and of `f t`

   362	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t : T'.left)

     8	/-!
     9	# The section rank at a chart-locus point
    10	
    11	`Pic0ChartLocusH0One` specializes the chart parameter to the genus and obtains the
    12	unique-effective-representative value `h⁰ = 1`.  This file records the unspecialized
    13	calculation.  If the chart parameter is `n` and the curve has Euler characteristic
    14	`1 - g`, the vanishing witness extracted from `chartLocus` has
    15	
    16	`h⁰ = n + 1 - g`.
    17	
    18	This separates two roles that a coverage argument must not conflate: a large parameter can
    19	force `H¹`-vanishing, while the injective Abel chart needs the genus parameter, where the
    20	same rank formula becomes `h⁰ = 1`.
    21	-/
    22

    27	universe u
    28

    39	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    40	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    41	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    42	
    43	noncomputable section
    44	
    45	/-- Chart-locus membership at parameter `n` supplies a witness of section rank `n + 1 - g` on a
    46	curve with Euler characteristic `1 - g`.
    47	
    48	The conclusion retains the presentation, divisor-class, degree, and vanishing clauses from
    49	`IsSplitWitness`; consequently it is tied to the given class and cannot be inhabited by an
    50	unrelated trivial divisor. -/
    51	theorem exists_splitting_h0_formula_of_mem_chartLocus
    52	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
    53	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (n g : ℕ)
    54	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    55	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    56	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    57	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0)
    58	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
    59	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
    60	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
    61	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
    62	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
    63	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    64	        (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
    65	      PicEtAff.map C L
    66	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
    67	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
    68	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
    69	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M ∧
    70	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) ∧
    71	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    72	        ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1) ∧
    73	      (Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) : ℤ)
    74	        = (n : ℤ) + 1 - (g : ℤ) := by
    75	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hWcl, hWh1⟩ := ht
    76	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
    77	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    78	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
    79	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    80	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
    81	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
    82	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
    83	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
    84	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
    85	  have hWdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) := by
    86	    rw [← classDeg_picClass (K := L) W, hWcl,
    87	      classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff C L _ M hM]
    88	    change degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) (Over.testPoint t) = (n : ℤ)
    89	    rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
    90	      degAt_sigmaFamily, hlam, hdeg]
    91	    ring
    92	  have hχL : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (g : ℤ) :=

    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` proves `isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` over an
    12	**affine** test, and its docstring says the general-test statement "follows from this one by the
    13	affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii) … needs no new mathematics".  That
    14	claim is right, and this file discharges it — but two of its ingredients were not where the tree
    15	said they were.
    16	
    17	## The advertised lemma that was absent
    18	
    19	`Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`'s header says chart-independence of the residue field is free
    20	"and the chart comparison becomes a lemma (`testPointField_affineOpen_iso`) instead of a side
    21	condition.  That is the whole reason this file is short."  **No declaration of that name exists
    22	anywhere in the workspace** — the only occurrence was that sentence (cf. I-0624:
    23	advertised-but-absent).  Since it is cited as the reason a side condition is unnecessary, it is
    24	load-bearing prose, so it is supplied here as `testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso`.
    25	
    26	It is genuinely cheap, but not for the reason the header gives: what makes it work is that
    27	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U` is an **open immersion** on carriers
    28	(`IsAffineOpen.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec`), and mathlib already knows the residue-field map of an
    29	open immersion is an isomorphism
    30	(`Scheme.instIsIsoCommRingCatResidueFieldMapOfIsOpenImmersion`).  So the comparison is an
    31	iso for a structural reason, not by a computation with `Spec.residueFieldIso`.
    32	
    33	## Locality: what "open in every affine piece" needs
    34	
    35	`isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open`-style bookkeeping is not quite enough, because the locus over the
    36	piece is a subset of a *different* space (`Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, not `T.left`).  The bridge is that
    37	`fromSpecAffine`'s carrier map is an open immersion with range `U`, so the image of the piece's
    38	locus is the intersection of `chartLocus` with `U` — that is what
    39	`chartLocus_inter_affineOpen_eq_image` records, and the openness statement then follows from
    40	openness of an open immersion's image.
    41	
    42	## Main declarations
    43	
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso` — **the absent advertised lemma**:
    45	  the residue-field comparison along an affine-open test object is an isomorphism.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` — hence the split-witness predicate
    47	  at a point of an affine piece agrees with the one at its image in `T`; this is transport (i)'s
    48	  hypothesis `hinv` **discharged** for the affine-piece maps (both directions), rather than
    49	  assumed.

   179	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST**, i.e. the statement `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring

   191	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)

    13	`RigidEngine4Assembly` instantiated on the **relative twisted sheaf**

   162	noncomputable abbrev relTwistPair := (relTwistPairData C R π g).pair

   164	  (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π))

   167	/-- **The rigid engine on the relative twisted sheaf** (Kleiman 3.10 (v)⟹(i)+(iii),
   168	curve-lite; worksheet §1.2 Level 2, all hypotheses discharged): if every residue-field
   169	fibre of `H¹` of the two-lattice pair of `F_g` vanishes (complex form — the sheaf-level
   170	discharge is the W6-full seam), then
   171	
   172	* `H¹(C_R, F_g) = 0`,
   173	* `H⁰(C_R, F_g)` is a finite projective `R`-module. -/
   174	theorem relTwistRigidEngine [IsNoetherianRing R]
   175	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
   176	      Subsingleton ((relTwistPair C R π g).H1 ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   177	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (relTwistSheaf C R (fiberTwoCover π) g) 1) ∧
   178	      Module.Finite R (Sheaf.HModule (relTwistSheaf C R (fiberTwoCover π) g) 0) ∧
   179	      Module.Projective R (Sheaf.HModule (relTwistSheaf C R (fiberTwoCover π) g) 0) := by
   180	  haveI := moduleFinite_aeval'_relTwistPair_t₀ C R π g hπ
   181	  haveI := moduleFinite_aeval'_relTwistPair_t₁ C R π g hπ
   182	  haveI := free_relTwistSections₀ C R π g
   183	  haveI := free_relTwistSections₁ C R π g
   184	  haveI := free_relTwistSectionsOverlap C R π g
   185	  exact (relTwistPairData C R π g).rigidEngine
   186	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
   187	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
   188	    (relCover_sup C R (fiberTwoCover π)) hfib
   189	
   190	include hπ in
   191	/-- **The openness export on the relative twisted sheaf** (the strata gift, worksheet
   192	§3.3): the fibrewise-vanishing locus of `H¹` of the pair of `F_g` is open in `Spec R`.
   193	Noetherian-free (COH-1 + RE-2). -/
   194	theorem relTwistRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing :
   195	    IsOpen {p : PrimeSpectrum R |
   196	      Subsingleton ((relTwistPair C R π g).H1 ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)} := by
   197	  haveI := moduleFinite_aeval'_relTwistPair_t₀ C R π g hπ
   198	  haveI := moduleFinite_aeval'_relTwistPair_t₁ C R π g hπ
   199	  exact (relTwistPairData C R π g).rigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing
   200	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
   201	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
   202	
   203	/-- **The module-coefficient clause on the relative twisted sheaf** (Kleiman `eq:Q`;
   204	worksheet §1.2 `h0_baseChange`): on the vanishing locus, formation of `H⁰(C_R, F_g)`
   205	commutes with `⊗_R P` for **every** `R`-module `P`. -/
   206	noncomputable def relTwistH0TensorEquiv
   207	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C R π g).H1)
   208	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] :
   209	    (Sheaf.HModule (relTwistSheaf C R (fiberTwoCover π) g) 0) ⊗[R] P ≃ₗ[R]
   210	      ↥(LinearMap.ker ((relTwistPair C R π g).diff.rTensor P)) := by
   211	  haveI := free_relTwistSectionsOverlap C R π g
   212	  exact (relTwistPairData C R π g).h0TensorEquiv
   213	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
   214	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
   215	    (relCover_sup C R (fiberTwoCover π)) hH1 P
   216	
   217	/-- **The ring-map base-change clause on the relative twisted sheaf, abstract half**
   218	(worksheet §1.2 `rigidEngine_baseChange`): on the vanishing locus,
   219	`R' ⊗[R] H⁰(C_R, F_g)` is `R'`-linearly the kernel of the base-changed Čech
   220	differential, for **every** `R`-algebra `R'`. Threading onto `H⁰` of the base-changed
   221	sheaf on the nose composes this with `RigidEngine.kerCongr` along the CBC-1 term
   222	identifications (`relTwistTermBaseChange₀/₁`, `relTwistOverlapBaseChange`) and the
   223	twisted δ-naturality square — the `RelativeH1BaseChange` frontier. -/
   224	noncomputable def relTwistH0BaseChangeEquiv
   225	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C R π g).H1)
   226	    (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R'] :
   227	    R' ⊗[R] (Sheaf.HModule (relTwistSheaf C R (fiberTwoCover π) g) 0) ≃ₗ[R']
   228	      ↥(LinearMap.ker ((relTwistPair C R π g).diff.baseChange R')) := by
   229	  haveI := free_relTwistSectionsOverlap C R π g
   230	  exact (relTwistPairData C R π g).h0BaseChangeEquiv
   231	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
   232	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
   233	    (relCover_sup C R (fiberTwoCover π)) hH1 R'
   234	
   235	include hπ in
   236	/-- **The vanishing hypothesis in pair form from the fibre form** — convenience wrapper:
   237	COH-1 + Nakayama propagation for the pair of `F_g` (Noetherian-free). Consumers holding
   238	the fibrewise hypothesis can use this to feed `relTwistH0TensorEquiv`/
   239	`relTwistH0BaseChangeEquiv`. -/
   240	theorem relTwist_subsingleton_pairH1
   241	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
   242	      Subsingleton ((relTwistPair C R π g).H1 ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   243	    Subsingleton (relTwistPair C R π g).H1 := by
   244	  haveI := moduleFinite_aeval'_relTwistPair_t₀ C R π g hπ
   245	  haveI := moduleFinite_aeval'_relTwistPair_t₁ C R π g hπ
   246	  haveI : Module.Finite R (relTwistPair C R π g).H1 :=
   247	    (relTwistPair C R π g).moduleFinite_h1
   248	  exact AlgebraicJacobian.RigidEngine.subsingleton_of_forall_subsingleton_residueField_tensor
   249	    hfib

     9	/-!
    10	# RE-4 — the ring-map base-change clause, threaded through CBC-1
    11	
    12	The last clause of the worksheet's Level-2 statement
    13	(`informal/w4-rigid-engine-worksheet.md` §1.2, `rigidEngine_baseChange`): on the
    14	vanishing locus, formation of the twisted `H⁰` commutes **on the nose** with every
    15	test-ring change `R → R'`, and the twisted `H¹` vanishes after base change.
    16	
    17	The abstract half (`relTwistH0BaseChangeEquiv`, `RigidEngine4Engine`) lands in the kernel
    18	of the base-changed Čech differential; this file threads it through the landed CBC-1 term
    19	identifications (`relTwistTermBaseChange₀/₁`, `relTwistOverlapBaseChange`,
    20	`RelativeH1BaseChange`) onto `H⁰` of the base-changed sheaf. The one genuinely new
    21	ingredient is **the twisted δ-naturality square** (`relTwistPairDiffBaseChange`) — the
    22	cocycle-conjugated analogue of the landed `relDiffBaseChange`, the frontier recorded in
    23	`RelativeH1BaseChange`'s module docstring: in trivialized coordinates the twisted
    24	differential is `(s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|ov − g · s₁|ov` (`twistTriv₀_pairDiff`), and the square is
    25	the same `relSectionsMap` bookkeeping with the extra `g`-factor carried through
    26	`map_mul` and `relCocycleBaseChange`.
    27	
    28	## Main declarations
    29	
    30	* `twistTriv₀_pairDiff` — the twisted Čech differential in trivialized coordinates.
    31	* `relTwistDomBaseChange` — CBC-1 for the degree-zero term of the twisted complex.
    32	* `relTwistPairDiffBaseChange` — **the twisted δ-naturality square**.
    33	* `relTwistH0BaseChange` — **`H⁰` base change on the nose**:
    34	  `R' ⊗[R] H⁰(C_R, F_g) ≃ₗ[R'] H⁰(C_{R'}, F_{g'})` on the vanishing locus, for every
    35	  test-ring change `R → R'` (`g' = relCocycleBaseChange g`).
    36	* `relTwist_subsingleton_h1_baseChange` — **`H¹` vanishes after base change**:
    37	  `Subsingleton H¹(C_{R'}, F_{g'})` on the vanishing locus.
    38	-/

    53	/-! ## The twisted differential in trivialized coordinates -/

    55	section Trivialized
    56	
    57	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    58	variable (V₀ V₁ : X.Opens) (g : Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ)
    59	
    60	/-- **The twisted Čech differential in trivialized coordinates**: under the chart-0
    61	trivialization of the overlap, `(p₀, p₁) ↦ p₀|ov − p₁|ov` becomes
    62	`(s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|ov − g · s₁|ov` (the `twistDefect` shape). -/
    63	lemma twistTriv₀_pairDiff (p₀ : ↥(twistSubmodule k V₀ V₁ g V₀))
    64	    (p₁ : ↥(twistSubmodule k V₀ V₁ g V₁)) :
    65	    twistTriv₀ k V₀ V₁ g (inf_le_left : V₀ ⊓ V₁ ≤ V₀)
    66	        (secRes (twistSheaf k V₀ V₁ g) (inf_le_left : V₀ ⊓ V₁ ≤ V₀) p₀
    67	          - secRes (twistSheaf k V₀ V₁ g) (inf_le_right : V₀ ⊓ V₁ ≤ V₁) p₁)
    68	      = X.resHom (inf_le_left : V₀ ⊓ V₁ ≤ V₀)
    69	            (twistTriv₀ k V₀ V₁ g (le_refl V₀) p₀)
    70	        - (g : Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)) *
    71	            X.resHom (inf_le_right : V₀ ⊓ V₁ ≤ V₁)
    72	              (twistTriv₁ k V₀ V₁ g (le_refl V₁) p₁) := by
    73	  rw [map_sub, secRes_twistSheaf, secRes_twistSheaf]
    74	  congr 1
    75	  · exact twistTriv₀_res k V₀ V₁ g inf_le_left (le_refl V₀) p₀
    76	  · rw [twistTriv₀_inf_eq]
    77	    exact congrArg (fun y => (g : Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)) * y)
    78	      (twistTriv₁_res k V₀ V₁ g inf_le_right (le_refl V₁) p₁)
    79

    82	/-! ## CBC-1 for the twisted complex -/

    84	section Square
    85

    13	2-chart `relTwistH0BaseChange` (`RigidEngine4BaseChange`). The abstract kernel clause
    14	`datumH0BaseChangeEquiv` (`GluedSheafEngine`) is threaded through the stage-(1d-ii) chart-term
    15	identifications `termBaseChange`/`termBaseChange_tmul` (`GluedSheafTermBaseChangeEquiv`) onto
    16	`H⁰` of the base-changed datum sheaf.
    17	
    18	* `termBaseChange₀`/`termBaseChange₁`/`termBaseChangeInf` — the chart-term base changes at the
    19	  two pinned charts and their overlap.
    20	* `datumDomBaseChange` — the base change of the two-cover degree-zero term
    21	  `F(V₀ᴮ) × F(V₁ᴮ)`.
    22	* `datumDiffBaseChange` — **the δ-naturality square** (the glued analogue of
    23	  `relTwistDiffBaseChange`; no cocycle conjugation — the componentwise restrictions commute
    24	  with `sectionsMap` through `gluedRes_sectionsMap`).
    25	* `datumH0BaseChange` — **`H⁰` base change on the nose**:
    26	  `B' ⊗[B] H⁰(C_B, F_D) ≃ₗ[B'] H⁰(C_{B'}, F_{D'})` on the vanishing locus, for every ring map
    27	  `B → B'` (`D' = D.baseChange B'`) — the on-the-nose form RE-5's DAT-B route consumes.
    28	* `datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange` — **`H¹` vanishes after base change** on the vanishing
    29	  locus.
    30	-/

   156	/-! ## The degree-zero term base change and the δ-naturality square -/
   157	
   158	/-- The base change of the two-cover degree-zero term `F(V₀ᴮ) × F(V₁ᴮ)`. -/
   159	noncomputable def datumDomBaseChange :
   160	    B' ⊗[B] ((D.sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)) ×
   161	        (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁))) ≃ₗ[B']
   162	      ((D.baseChange B').sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B' (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)) ×
   163	        ((D.baseChange B').sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B' (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)) :=
   164	  (TensorProduct.prodRight B B' B' _ _).trans
   165	    ((D.termBaseChange₀ B').prodCongr (D.termBaseChange₁ B'))
   166	
   167	/-- The degree-zero term base change on a pure tensor. -/
   168	lemma datumDomBaseChange_tmul (b' : B')
   169	    (p : (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)) ×
   170	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁))) :
   171	    D.datumDomBaseChange B' (b' ⊗ₜ[B] p) =
   172	      (D.termBaseChange₀ B' (b' ⊗ₜ[B] p.1), D.termBaseChange₁ B' (b' ⊗ₜ[B] p.2)) := by
   173	  rw [datumDomBaseChange, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, TensorProduct.prodRight_tmul]
   174	  rfl
   175	
   176	set_option maxHeartbeats 4000000 in
   177	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   178	/-- **The δ-naturality square** (the glued analogue of `relTwistDiffBaseChange`): the base
   179	change of the datum's Čech differential over `B` is carried to the datum's Čech differential
   180	over `B'` under the term identifications. There is no cocycle conjugation — the componentwise
   181	restrictions commute with `sectionsMap` through `gluedRes_sectionsMap`. -/
   182	theorem datumDiffBaseChange
   183	    (x : B' ⊗[B] ((D.sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)) ×
   184	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)))) :
   185	    D.termBaseChangeInf B' (((datumPair D).diff).baseChange B' x) =
   186	      (datumPair (D.baseChange B')).diff (D.datumDomBaseChange B' x) := by
   187	  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   188	  | zero => simp only [map_zero]
   189	  | add a b ha hb => simp only [map_add, ha, hb]
   190	  | tmul b' p =>
   191	    have hbc : ((datumPair D).diff).baseChange B' (b' ⊗ₜ[B] p) =
   192	        b' ⊗ₜ[B] (datumPair D).diff p := LinearMap.baseChange_tmul _ _ _
   193	    rw [hbc]
   194	    simp only [D.datumDomBaseChange_tmul B', TwoLatticePair.diff_apply,
   195	      D.termBaseChange₀_tmul B', D.termBaseChange₁_tmul B']
   196	    rw [TensorProduct.tmul_sub, map_sub, D.termBaseChangeInf_tmul B',
   197	      D.termBaseChangeInf_tmul B', map_smul, map_smul]
   198	    congr 1
   199	    · congr 1
   200	      exact (D.gluedRes_sectionsMap B'
   201	        (inf_le_left : (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   202	          (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
   203	        (le_preimage_chart B' (fiberTwoCover π).V₀)
   204	        (le_preimage_chart B' ((fiberTwoCover π).V₀ ⊓ (fiberTwoCover π).V₁))
   205	        (inf_le_left : (relCover C B' (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   206	          (relCover C B' (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C B' (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
   207	        p.1).symm
   208	    · congr 1
   209	      exact (D.gluedRes_sectionsMap B'
   210	        (inf_le_right : (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   211	          (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
   212	        (le_preimage_chart B' (fiberTwoCover π).V₁)
   213	        (le_preimage_chart B' ((fiberTwoCover π).V₀ ⊓ (fiberTwoCover π).V₁))
   214	        (inf_le_right : (relCover C B' (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   215	          (relCover C B' (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C B' (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
   216	        p.2).symm

   218	/-! ## The on-the-nose H⁰ base change and H¹ vanishing -/
   219	
   220	open AlgebraicJacobian
   221	
   222	/-- **`H⁰` base change on the nose** (DAT-1 (1d-ii) tail; the RE-5/DAT-B transport interface):
   223	on the vanishing locus, for every ring map `B → B'`,
   224	
   225	`B' ⊗[B] H⁰(C_B, F_D) ≃ₗ[B'] H⁰(C_{B'}, F_{D'})`
   226	
   227	with `D' = D.baseChange B'` — the abstract kernel clause `datumH0BaseChangeEquiv` threaded
   228	through the term identifications by the δ-naturality square `datumDiffBaseChange`. -/
   229	noncomputable def datumH0BaseChange (hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1) :
   230	    B' ⊗[B] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ≃ₗ[B']
   231	      Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange B').sheaf 0 :=
   232	  (datumH0BaseChangeEquiv D hH1 B').trans
   233	    ((RigidEngine.kerCongr ((datumPair D).diff.baseChange B')
   234	        ((datumPair (D.baseChange B')).diff)
   235	        (D.datumDomBaseChange B') (D.termBaseChangeInf B')
   236	        (fun x => D.datumDiffBaseChange B' x)).trans
   237	      ((D.baseChange B').pairData.h0Equiv
   238	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B' (fiberTwoCover π))
   239	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B' (fiberTwoCover π))
   240	        (relCover_sup C B' (fiberTwoCover π))).symm)
   241	
   242	/-- **`H¹` vanishes after base change** on the vanishing locus: the base-changed Čech
   243	differential is surjective (right-exactness of `B' ⊗[B] -` plus the δ-square), so `H¹` of the
   244	base-changed datum sheaf vanishes. -/
   245	theorem datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange (hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1) :
   246	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange B').sheaf 1) := by
   247	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (datumPair D).diff :=
   248	    D.pairData.surjective_diff (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover π))
   249	      (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover π)) hH1
   250	  have hbc : Function.Surjective ((datumPair D).diff.baseChange B') := by
   251	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
   252	    exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective B' hsurj
   253	  have hsurj' : Function.Surjective (datumPair (D.baseChange B')).diff :=
   254	    RigidEngine.surjective_congr _ _ (D.datumDomBaseChange B') (D.termBaseChangeInf B')
   255	      (fun x => D.datumDiffBaseChange B' x) hbc
   256	  haveI : Subsingleton (datumPair (D.baseChange B')).H1 := by
   257	    have h : (datumPair (D.baseChange B')).imageLattice = ⊤ := by
   258	      rw [← (datumPair (D.baseChange B')).range_diff_eq, LinearMap.range_eq_top]
   259	      exact hsurj'
   260	    rw [TwoLatticePair.H1, h]
   261	    infer_instance
   262	  exact ((D.baseChange B').pairData.h1Equiv
   263	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B' (fiberTwoCover π))
   264	    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B' (fiberTwoCover π))
   265	    (relCover_sup C B' (fiberTwoCover π))).toEquiv.subsingleton
   266

    10	/-!
    11	# Chart-term base change of the glued sheaf: the comparison and its localizations
    12	(DAT-1, stage 1d-ii, terms — part 1)
    13	
    14	On a pinned chart open `V` carrying a finite subordinate trivializing basic-open family,
    15	this file builds the comparison `Ψ : A' ⊗[A] F_D(V_B) →ₗ[A'] F_{D'}(V_{B'})`
    16	(`A := Γ(V_B)`, `A' := Γ(V_{B'})`, the `liftBaseChange` of the componentwise
    17	`sectionsMap`) and proves the piece-level localization identification that stage
    18	(1d-ii)'s bijectivity argument consumes:
    19	
    20	* `termFamily`/`termFamily_le`/`termFamily_span`/`termFamily_cover` — the base-changed
    21	  trivializing family (images under `relSectionsMap`), subordinate to the base-changed
    22	  pieces, spanning the unit ideal.
    23	* `sectionsMapₗ` — the comparison as an `A`-linear map (`A` acting on the target
    24	  through the chart-ring comparison).
    25	* `termPieceLocalized` — **the piece-level identification**: composing the comparison
    26	  `Ψ` with the piece restriction `F'(V_{B'}) → F'(D(h'ᵢ))` is a localization of
    27	  `A' ⊗[A] F(V_B)` at the powers of `h i` — through the piece trivializations, the
    28	  target is `Γ'(D(h'ᵢ))`, free of rank one, and the composite matches the
    29	  tensor-of-localizations of the source.
    30	
    31	Part 2 (`GluedSheafTermBaseChangeEquiv`) assembles these into the on-the-nose
    32	equivalence `B' ⊗[B] F(V_B) ≃ₗ[B'] F'(V_{B'})` by span-locality.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	set_option autoImplicit false
    36	/- Statements mix `Γ(relCurve C B, ·)` with opens produced on the product spelling
    37	`(C ⊗ overSpec k B).left`; see `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RelativeSectionsLinear`. -/
    38	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    39	
    40	universe u
    41	
    42	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory TopologicalSpace
    43	open Opposite
    44	
    45	open scoped TensorProduct
    46	
    47	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    48	
    49	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    50	
    51	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    52	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    53	variable (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B'] [IsScalarTower k B B']
    54	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
    55	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
    56	
    57	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
    58	
    59	section Terms
    60	
    61	variable (V : C.left.Opens)
    62	
    63	/-- (Implementation) The chart inclusion of the base-changed open into the
    64	comparison-preimage. -/
    65	lemma le_preimage_chart :
    66	    (fst C (overSpec k B')).left ⁻¹ᵁ V ≤
    67	      relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
    68	  (relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V).ge
    69	
    70	variable {ι : Type u} (σ : ι → D.index)
    71	variable (h : ι → Γ(relCurve C B, (fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
    72	
    73	/-- The base-changed trivializing family: the images of the generators under the
    74	sections comparison. -/
    75	noncomputable def termFamily (i : ι) :
    76	    Γ(relCurve C B', (fst C (overSpec k B')).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=

     8	/-!
     9	# Canonical pushforward base change for scheme modules
    10	
    11	For a cartesian square of schemes, `canonicalBaseChangeMap` is the Beck--Chevalley mate
    12	
    13	```text
    14	g^* f_* M --> f'_* (g')^* M.
    15	```
    16	
    17	The two coherence theorems identify its pullback followed by the counit with the pullback of
    18	the original counit.  Invertibility is deliberately not asserted here: it is a property of the
    19	module and square, not part of the construction of the canonical map.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory Limits
    27	
    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    29	
    30	/-- The canonical Beck--Chevalley mate for pushforward along a cartesian square. -/
    31	noncomputable def canonicalBaseChangeMap
    32	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    33	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    34	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    35	    Scheme.Modules.pushforward f ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback g ⟶
    36	      Scheme.Modules.pullback g' ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f' :=
    37	  CategoryTheory.mateEquiv
    38	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f)
    39	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f')
    40	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    41	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    42	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom)
    43	
    44	/-- Pulling back the canonical mate and evaluating recovers its defining pullback telescope. -/
    45	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit
    46	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    47	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    48	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    49	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    50	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    51	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M) =
    52	      ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    53	        Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    54	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).hom).app
    55	          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    56	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    57	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    58	  rw [canonicalBaseChangeMap]
    59	  exact CategoryTheory.mateEquiv_counit _ _ _ M
    60	
    61	/-- After cancelling the pullback telescope, the base-changed counit is the pulled-back
    62	original counit. -/
    63	theorem canonicalBaseChangeMap_counit_cancel
    64	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    65	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    66	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (M : X.Modules) :
    67	    ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
    68	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
    69	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g' f).symm).inv).app
    70	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M)) ≫
    71	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f').map ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app M) ≫
    72	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
    73	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj M)) =
    74	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map
    75	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).counit.app M) := by
    76	  erw [canonicalBaseChangeMap_pullback_counit]
    77	  erw [Iso.inv_hom_id_app_assoc]
    78	  rfl
    79	
    80	end AlgebraicGeometry

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",
